messages.author: 373ead540701665c
messages.subject: Re: Differences Between SPSS and Lavaan Correlations.
parts:
Thank you.  At issue here is the correlation between variables "F" and "G".  In SPSS, this correlation is reported as 0.57.  However, in lavaan, it is reported as 0.53.  Note, however, that the correlations between "D" and "E" are identical between SPSS and lavaan (i.e., 0.41).

Please see attached for (1) a file containing the data in question, (2) a file containing SPSS syntax for the correlation between variables "F" and "G", (3) R output containing the correlation in question, and (4) lavaan syntax.

Any assistance in determining why the F ~~ G correlation differs between SPSS and lavaan is highly appreciated. 

My lavaan syntax is as follows:

model <- '  F ~ d*D + f*E

G ~ e*D

A ~ a*F + c*G

B ~ b*A

B ~ C 

D ~~ E

G ~~ F

B  ~    g*G

               ind1 := a*b

               ind2 := c*b

               ind3 := d*a*b

               ind4 := e*c*b

               ind5 := f*a*b

               ind6 := e*g'

fit<-sem(model,Dataset,fixed.x=FALSE)

summary(fit)

inspect(fit, 'r2')

standardizedsolution(fit)

modindices(fit)

fitmeasures(fit)

F G     -0.570   -0.637   -0.495

. corrci D E
(obs=351)

D E      0.411    0.320    0.494

HTH.

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: Differences Between SPSS and Lavaan Correlations.
parts:
The issue isn't a lavaan (or SPSS) specific one. In your lavaan code both F and G are outcome variables. So the covariance between F and G in your model results is a residual covariance (and the correlations are residual correlations). There's no reason to expect that the residual covariance and the bivariate correlation are the same. If you look at the sample statistics lavaan is using in your models the correlation is the same:
cov2cor(inspect(fit, "sampstats")$cov)## gives the correlation between F and G of -.57

The other thing to note, is that your model has non-zero df, so the model implied covariance matrix and the data covariance matrix are different. In the model implied matrix, the correlation between F and G is different from the correlation in the data.
cov2cor(fitted(fit)$cov) ##the correlation in the model implied matrix is -.548

Alex
